To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most common trajectory was characterized by a low ERI level, and that this trajectory was dominated by men, while all other trajectories were dominated by female employees.

a sizeable portion of employees in Sweden experienced ERI at work and the most favourable trajectory was characterised by relatively more men and better work-related characteristics, whereas the less favourable ERIES trajectories were characterised by relatively less favourable work-related characteristics.

a large proportion of Swedish employees experience imbalance between efforts at work and the rewards they receive, that these imbalances change over time and that these changes are associated with changes in health.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the dynamics and consequences of ERI, and we conclude that it is important to monitor the development of imbalance in employees, and that the development of ERI may be a useful indicator of the need for interventions.
a group of employees who are at high risk of developing ERI and who are at risk for impaired health.
the development of effort-reward balance over time and the associations between trajectories of ERI and health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERI is a risk factor for poor health.

the majority of the participants had low ERI, but that a considerable minority had ERI and that the less favourable trajectories of ERI were associated with worse health and more sickness absence than the stable low ERI trajectory.
the ERI trajectories are associated with health and that the less favourable trajectories associate with worse health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a sizeable group of workers are exposed to imbalance between efforts and reward and that this imbalance may be a risk factor for poor health and sickness absence.
the ERI concept is useful to understand the development of work-related health problems in the Swedish population.
ERI is a dynamic concept, which may be associated with health.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ERI is an important factor in health inequalities and in the development of health over time, which should be taken into account when planning interventions and policies to improve health in working populations.
a large proportion of the population is exposed to imbalance between efforts and reward at work, which is associated with adverse health outcomes.
a sizeable number of workers in Sweden experience a mismatch between their efforts and rewards at their jobs and that this imbalance is associated with adverse health outcomes.
